converge-review-replay.text: On hang restart, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard is always False for spawn-context processes (SpawnProcess), so kill() never runs. This allows old processes to keep running while replacements start on the same shards, causing duplicate segment reads and up to 10 orphaned processes per index holding Redis and Kafka connections.

In join(), terminate() is behind the same wrong isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, so it never runs for SpawnProcess. On shutdown or rebalance, flusher processes are never terminated.

In join(), once the deadline passes, the 'remaining_time <= 0: break' exits the loop before terminate() runs for the current process and all later ones, creating a gap once the isinstance guard bug is fixed.

Each process gets its own SpansBuffer(shards) holding only its subset of shards, so ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) is computed per process. This makes spans.buffer.max-flush-segments silently become a per-process budget, scaling total flush per cycle with process count and delaying backpressure.

The parent keeps one SpansBuffer per child, and every submit() loops over all of them, causing N record_stored_segments pipelines and N cluster-wide get_memory_info INFO calls against the same Redis cluster instead of one, adding unnecessary I/O on the consumer main thread.
_create_process_for_shard (lines 127-132) has no callers and is dead code since restarts go through _create_process_for_shards.
'if not process: continue' can never be true since self.processes only holds started Process or Thread objects which are always truthy.
Inconsistent metric tag key: lines 185 and 195 use 'shard' while line 199 (spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) uses 'shards'.

The 'shard' tag value at lines 185 and 195 is a comma-joined list of a process's shards which changes on every rebalance and has high cardinality, while line 244 tags a single int under the same key and existing buffer metrics use 'shard_i' for this concept.
The docstring says 'Creates one process per shard' but the CLI default --flusher-processes=1 runs a single process for all shards in production.

converge-review-atomic.text: After the first partition rebalance, messages in thread-queue-parallel mode are dropped without being processed, and their offsets are still committed, causing silent data loss. The factory builds one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and hands it to every strategy. On revoke, close() and join() call queue_pool.shutdown(), but factory.queue_pool is not reset, so the next strategy's submit() reaches work_queue.put() which raises queue.ShutDown. The broad except then marks the offset complete, and the commit loop commits it.

The arroyo commit callback is called from the background _commit_loop thread instead of the consumer thread, so it races with StreamProcessor's poll and rebalance handling. KafkaConsumer's staged-offset state is not thread-safe. On revoke, the commit thread is joined with only a 5s timeout, so it can still commit for a partition this consumer no longer owns.

There is no backpressure. The queues are unbounded (created with queue.Queue() and no maxsize) and submit() never raises MessageRejected, so memory grows without limit under consumer lag. OffsetTracker all_offsets/outstanding also grow without limit, and each WorkItem holds the full Message.

On close/join, work already queued is abandoned. FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before shutting down the queues, so each worker exits after its current item and does not drain its queue, which defeats immediate=False. The next partition owner reprocesses the abandoned items.

close()/join() stop the commit thread without a final get_committable_offsets()/commit, so up to about 1s of completed work goes uncommitted on every revoke and graceful shutdown. This breaks arroyo's join contract to finish submitted work and commit it, resulting in at-least-once duplicates.

converge-review-verified.text: The change defines `self.downsize` twice. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the first `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Every caller using the old 5-argument form now raises ArgumentError, so custom emoji resizing breaks silently in Sidekiq. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which is 5 arguments to a method that takes 3..4.

The client-side size check replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` for every upload type. Attachments between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10 MB now pass in the browser and are then rejected by the server. Sites with limits above 10240 KB are capped by a limit the admin never set. Only images needed the limit relaxed.

The HTTP 413 handler now always tells the user the limit is 10240 KB. A 413 comes from nginx or another proxy, whose limit is whatever the operator configured, so the message misstates the real limit on many installs.

The API URL-download cap changed from `max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, regardless of type or site settings. It duplicates the nginx `client_max_body_size 10m` in a third place with no setting behind it. On sites with limits above 10 MB, larger API URL uploads are truncated rather than cleanly rejected.

With `allow_animated_thumbnails` on, an oversized GIF is routed to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects a WxH geometry, so gifsicle should exit non-zero and `convert_with` returns false. The loop then burns all 5 attempts and the upload is still rejected.

converge-review.text: The cron cancel loop wraps sequential awaited SendGrid cancel requests in one try/catch and queues row deletes as lazy Prisma promises that only run at the final Promise.all. One failed cancel aborts the loop: none of the queued deletes run, including those whose batch was already cancelled, and later cancelled reminders are not processed. A persistently failing row blocks every reminder queued behind it until its scheduledDate passes.

Deferred cancellation only sets cancelled=true and relies on the 15-minute cron, which cancels only reminders due within the next hour. A booking cancelled less than about 15 minutes before its reminder's send time (after the last cron pass) still gets the reminder email, whereas before the patch cancellation was immediate.

Reminder cleanup is now fire-and-forget: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls inside forEach are not awaited. The cancelled=true write or row delete can be lost when the request ends (serverless freeze), and failures are only console-logged, so the reminder may still be sent.

Immediate SendGrid cancels on workflow deletion, step deletion and reschedule may exceed a SendGrid limit on concurrently cancelled or paused batches, causing later cancels to fail and emails to be sent.

Prisma is imported but no longer used, breaking unused-imports/no-unused-imports (error). PrismaPromise is now a value import but used only as a type, breaking @typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports (error). Line 9 lacks the trailing comma required by prettier.

The import type { App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma } was folded into a value import, though all four names are used only as types, breaking @typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports (error) in handleNewBooking.ts.
The new import { Prisma, WorkflowReminder } from '@calcom/prisma/client' imports names used only as types, breaking @typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports (error) in scheduleEmailReminders.ts.
The new try/catch wraps a forEach of un-awaited async calls whose callees already catch their own errors, so log.error in the catch at handleNewBooking.ts:964-975 is unreachable.

twilio.cancelSMS and the row delete share one try block. If cancelSMS throws (e.g., the message was already sent), the row is not deleted, whereas old callers deleted the row whatever Twilio returned.
The patch uses prisma.workflowReminder.delete where callers previously used deleteMany. delete throws P2025 when the row is already gone (e.g., racing a cascade delete), causing log noise.

The boolean immediateDelete parameter makes one function do two unrelated jobs: cancel at SendGrid without touching the DB, or flag in the DB only. The name is misleading because it deletes nothing, and relies on an undocumented precondition that the caller cascade-deletes the row.
The SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel request is duplicated in the cron and in emailReminderManager.ts:214-221, and the copies can drift.
The EMAIL/SMS reminder-deletion dispatch block is copied at 7 call sites, and the patch had to edit every copy.
No tests cover the new cancel lifecycle (flag on cancel, cron cancels at SendGrid, row deleted) or the reschedule paths.

The cron cancel loop runs sequential `await client.request(...)` calls inside one try/catch. One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the loop, so every later cancelled reminder goes uncancelled in that run. If the same row keeps failing, later rows stay stuck until its scheduledDate passes, and their emails are sent.

Row deletes are queued as lazy Prisma promises and run only at `Promise.all` (about line 74). Any throw in the loop skips them, including deletes for reminders whose SendGrid batch was already cancelled. Those rows stay `cancelled: true` and are cancelled again on the next run.
The `try/catch` at lines 964-975 can never catch anything, so `log.error` at line 974 is dead code. It wraps a `forEach` over async calls that are not awaited.
About 60 lines of whitespace-only re-indentation inside a `/* ... */` commented-out block are unrelated to the fix and add noise to the diff and to git blame.
